chapter: Boyhood in Webster Groves and early roadhouse work
title: Roadhouse pay, tips and the Crystal Slipper area
summary: Money from the roadhouse helped with Lincoln. Older musicians took part of the tips. The place stood across from the Crystal Slipper, and Thomas says the lurid things people imagine did not happen.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Well, when you worked this thing at the roadhouse, were able to earn you earned a bit of money. I was wondering whether you/earned much to help with going to Lincoln.
Yes. I tell you what happened. My first year there , as I remember, we did pretty good. And, naturally put it in on buying ...
Now this was the summer before you went to Lincoln, was it?

Now you've got me a little confused. No, this could have been. It's around that same time because when I went to Lincoln I still had these short pants on, you know. It's around that same period. The money was fabulous accroding to what you

think about money. I mean for me, for a kid. Wasn't that much money, not really. And, there were things called they called tips. You had the kitty (?) box and you had the kitty and the guys, the older guys figured a kid doesn't need that much money so I guess they took some off for-themselves but they treat me very nicely, I thought. And there was the guy that owned the place, he was a tremendous guy. His family lived there.
Did this roadhouse have a name?
Yes, it did. It was across from a place called I think it was the Crystal Slipper. It's been a long time.
It's not a famous place, is it?

No, but things happened there that are tremendous. All these girls that I'm going to run into, all this booze I'm going to drinking at 12 years old, you know, didn't happen. We had lunch, we had a snack -- I had a snack with the kids before the kids went to bed. I'm a kid, you know. It was beautiful. It was tremendous. And, I'm in my second year there, I mean my second time in doing the, going to school.
Oh, of course, you'd come back from Lincoln in the summer?
And then you could go there?
